chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Ziyad ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever is not certain that one washing in wudu (ablution) suffices him will not be rewarded for the two.

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.تُجْزِئُهُ: is sufficient for him and fulfills the requirement

ai.seo_question: Does repeating the washing in wudu (ablution) bring reward if one does not believe a single washing is sufficient?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that in wudu (ablution), one must recognize that a single washing fulfills the obligation. If a person performs two washings without certainty that one is sufficient, he does not receive reward for doing the second.
